summary.text: Early forms are interpreted as grain above a person carrying it, and Shang inscriptions attest 年 in a harvest context. The character later came to mean “year,” though the steps between those meanings are not fully dated.

formation.text: The supported early construction is pictographic: 禾 and a human figure form a scene associated with harvesting grain. Some accounts also assign a sound role to the lower figure, but that analysis remains disputed. The later analysis of 禾 plus phonetic 千 is a traditional dictionary account, not confirmation of the earliest graph’s structure.

components.text: 禾 is the grain plant above the person. In the early graph, it forms part of the harvest scene.
The lower figure is interpreted as a person, 人, carrying grain. A sound role has also been proposed, but remains disputed.

sound_limitation.text: Current Mandarin readings 人 rén and 年 nián can be compared, but this modern pair does not establish a historical phonetic role for 人 in 年.

sound.text: In current Mandarin, 人 is rén and 年 is nián; this is a modern comparison only.

history.text: A selected oracle-bone-style form shows grain above a human-shaped figure. It is a modern rendering and illustrates the pictorial interpretation rather than proving a sound role for the lower element.

Later accounts describe the lower element as changing from 人 to 千 and record the analysis of 年 as 禾 plus phonetic 千. One account calls this change a misformation; the proposed sequence has not been checked against a dated run of glyph forms.

uncertainties.text: Whether the early lower figure 人 also served as a phonetic component remains disputed. No supplied comparison establishes its historical reading in 年; the reconstruction for 年 alone does not identify a sound component.

senses.text: In an oracle-bone divination, 年 is interpreted as the harvest the speaker hopes to receive. Another cited Shang example is also read as harvest.

senses.period: Shang use is reported; later Western Zhou examples are cited
senses.text: A grain cycle may have come to stand for a year. A possible Shang time-count use is reported with a caution about its reading, and Western Zhou bronze inscriptions use 年 in wishes for long duration; these examples do not date every step in the development.

senses.period: Shang and Zhou usage as described in the source; absolute dates unresolved
senses.text: One account distinguishes 年 as harvest, 歲 as harvest season, and 祀 as a regnal-year count in a Shang inscription. It reports that Zhou usage later replaced 祀 with 年 for regnal dating.
New Year is documented as a sense, but its emergence and development from the harvest meaning are not dated here.
年 is used for a person's age. The cited definitions do not establish when or how this use developed.

developments.text: The proposed development is that a successful grain cycle came to represent a year. The evidence does not establish the complete chronology.

limitations.text: The documented later senses are not all connected by established developments; dictionary listings alone do not supply their chronology.

items.period: Shang dynasty; oracle-bone script style, modern vector rendering of a Xiaoxuetang glyph identified as 42.F100, 甲2827 合27941
items.caption: An oracle-bone form of 年 has a branching grain-like element above a human-shaped lower element. It illustrates the interpretation of grain carried by a person in an early harvest context.
items.alt: Black oracle-bone-style graph on white, with a branching upper form above a separate human-shaped lower form.
items.selection_reason: The visible form is legible and matches the sourced interpretation of 年 as grain above a person associated with harvest. The pictorial reading does not establish whether the lower element also had a phonetic role.
items.rights: The Commons description states CC0 1.0 for the Xiaoxuetang glyph image and public-domain status for the modern vector representation. Modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

limitations.text: The image is a modern redraw. Whether the lower 人 also served as a sound component remains disputed, and the reported change to 千 has not been verified against a dated sequence of inspected forms.
